new_findings.contract: debug hook count counts Lua instruction dispatches; it is not a wall-clock timer and has no autonomous Client pump in the closed producer set.

Hook registry lookup is keyed by the currently executing thread. newthread copies native mask/count/callback fields but does not copy the per-thread Lua hook table entry in the captured construction path.

The two input alias closures read stack index -1; number/string convert through x87 FISTP; Lua boolean/other tags go to native zero. For SetKeymapEnabled, native nonzero enables input by clearing mask bit 2; native zero sets bit 2.

Both closures return C result count 1 but their converter/native calls do not push a new Lua result on the successful captured path; the caller must not treat the echoed last argument as an enable/runner acknowledgement.
ChangeKeymapType native accepts 0/1, copies 40 vector rows from FB8834+type*0x280 to FB8D34, and has no controller+58 or Q+2C store in that captured operation.

The raw-backed .text/.rdata/.data absolute FB73EC literal census yields one operand: constructor zero store. Q tick checks relative +2C only after setting controller+58, so pause would not free ordinary input even if a legal writer were later found.

Represent Lua instruction hook events separately from elapsed milliseconds or Client frames in offline tooling.
Enforce numeric input-alias arguments and never use returned argument as input-ready or scene-complete evidence.

List Server authoritative rules and state/reply/cancel behavior within already-proven entity/quest protocols as Server development requirements. Unresolved Client trigger/query/result-observer or callback interfaces remain Client reverse-engineering gaps; do not invent wire support.
